title: Travis Head hits back at Australia greats for firing a ‘bullet through’ current Test players | Australia cricket team | The Guardian
description: Australia’s vice-captain said it is unfair for former players to criticise modern batting lineup while he is eager to open in Tests against South Africa
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Australia’s vice-captain said it is unfair for former players to criticise modern batting lineup while he is eager to open in Tests against South Africa
Content: Travis Head has backed Australia’s current batting lineup before the Test series in South Africa starting in Durban on Friday.Photograph: Gerhard Duraan/Gallo Images/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTravis Head has backed Australia’s current batting lineup before the Test series in South Africa starting in Durban on Friday.Photograph: Gerhard Duraan/Gallo Images/Getty ImagesAustralia cricket teamTravis Head hits back at Australia greats for firing a ‘bullet through’ current Test playersOpener said it is unfair for ex-players to criticise modern batting lineupAustralia’s vice-captain eager to open in Tests against South AfricaAustralian Associated PressWed 7 Oct 2026 17.25 EDTLast modified on Wed 7 Oct 2026 17.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTravis Head has accused Australia’s golden generation of being unfair in “putting a bullet through” current players, saying the game has changed significantly since they played.Just a day after Matthew Hayden slammed selectors and accused them of promoting “the greatest pile of mediocrity” aftercalling up Nic Maddinson, Head took his own stand in South Africa.What’s left to say about Australia’s ball-tampering? The answer is everything | Geoff LemonRead moreAustralia’s vice-captain refused to make reference to particular critics or comments, but took issue with commentary around the team’s batting at a time when averages have dropped worldwide.Head also noted the current side had been through a “sticky situation” with the group of past players, in a clear nod to Justin Langer’s dramatic exit as coach in 2022.“I think it’s unfairly judged a fair bit from a group of past players, pretty much, that put the bullet through a lot of players,” Head said ahead of Friday’sfirst Test against South Africain Durban.“But that’s what they’re paid to do. Some of them need a job, so they go after us and that’s totally fine. This group is strong enough to deal with those sort of things. That’s how it is.“It’s unfortunate sometimes to have some of that feedback from a generation of players that we have huge respect for, but that’s the caper.”View image in fullscreenTravis Head trains in the nets before Australia meet South Africa in the first Test in Durban.Photograph: Gerhard Duraan/Gallo Images/Getty ImagesThe suggestion of a generational split between Australia’s two best eras of the past 50 years has long bubbled away, particularly since Langer’s exit after his side’s 2021-22 Ashes win, when he rejected a contract offer of only six months.Australia have remained the No 1 team in the world for the vast majority of that period, winning aWorld Test Championshipand keeping hold of the Ashes.“They’re a very proud bunch of guys,” Head said. “We went through a bit of a sticky situation a few years ago where they stood up and were pretty proud about one of their own [Langer].“But in saying that, we’re all one of each. We’re all each other. We play for the same cause. We have huge respect for it.“It’s always a balancing act with the, I guess, what they say and how you take it.”Test batting averages have dropped by close to 20 per cent from the end of the 2010s, while the Sheffield Shield has witnessed a similar downturn since the mid-2000s.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWhile critics have pointed to the drop in averages coinciding with the rise of T20 cricket, Head pointed to conditions as a major factor.He used Darren Lehmann’s record Sheffield Shield runs tally as an example of the changes, with the top 10 in history all playing across the turn of the century.In the time since, wickets have become harder to bat on and more drop-in pitches have been used, to the point whereCricketAustralia have now asked curators to err more towards batters.“It’s pretty obvious to see what the wickets were like back then to now,” Head said. “We have huge respect for what’s come before us, but it’s a completely different game.“Sometimes it’s commented around unfairly on some of the wickets that teams have played on, whether that be Sheffield Shield, Test cricket.“We’ve seen games go quicker than ever. We’ve got a lot of stats that suggest that the ball’s doing a lot more.”Head also said he would continue to open the batting in South Africa, and indicated he was miffed by some of the commentary around whether he should stay there.Explore more on these topicsAustralia cricket teamCricketAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Southampton manager Tonda Eckert given six-week suspended ban for Spygate scandal | Southampton | The Guardian
description: An Independent commission cited ‘genuine contrition’ but the FA wanted a three-month ban and may appeal
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: An Independent commission cited ‘genuine contrition’ but the FA wanted a three-month ban and may appeal
Content: Tonda Eckert took over as Southampton’s manager in December 2025.Photograph: Lee Keuneke/PAView image in fullscreenTonda Eckert took over as Southampton’s manager in December 2025.Photograph: Lee Keuneke/PASouthamptonSouthampton manager Tonda Eckert given six-week suspended ban for Spygate scandalIndependent commission cites ‘genuine contrition’But FA wanted three-month ban and may appealMatt HughesWed 7 Oct 2026 14.53 EDTFirst published on Wed 7 Oct 2026 11.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Southampton head coach, Tonda Eckert, has escaped a ban from the Football Association for his part in theSpygate scandalthat led to the club being expelled from last season’s Championship playoff final and denied the chance to win promotion to the Premier League.The German has been given a six-week suspended ban and £28,000 fine by an independent commission after admitting all charges of misconduct, but the FA could appeal against the sanction after its lawyers demanded a three-month ban from all football.Football Daily | Tears, drone ads and a 1,740-word manifesto: Messi v Ronaldo gets one more chapterRead moreQuick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Eckert was charged with misconduct in July afterSouthamptonadmitted they had spied on three Championship clubs last season in a breach of English Football League regulations, including their playoff semi-final opponents Middlesbrough before the first leg.Southampton beat Middlesbrough over two legs to reach the final, but were subsequently found guilty of a “contrived and determined plan” to spy on Oxford, Ipswich and Middlesbrough by an EFL independent disciplinary commission, who removed the club from the playoffs and imposed a four-point deduction for this season.While Southampton appealed against that punishment it was upheld by the league arbitration panel two days before the playoff final at Wembley, where Hull beat Middlesbrough to reach the Premier League.In their written reasons for imposing a suspended ban the independent commission makes clear they disagreed with many of the findings of the EFL panels, describing Eckert as a “particularly impressive witness” who showed “genuine contrition”.In contrast the original EFL commission that kicked Southampton out of the playoffs had condemned Eckert’s “deplorable” behaviour in pressuring junior members of staff to spy on their opponent’s training sessions, while they also said they were “unimpressed” with his testimony.The commission hearing the FA charges concluded there was no evidence of Eckert pressurising staff however, adding that “although there are three rule breaches, we do not consider there was a systematic or organised course of conduct”. With Eckert having admitted three breaches of FA Rule E3.1, most of the hearing, which took place last month, was devoted to determining the sanction.In their submission to the commission the FA’s lawyers initially argued for a ban from football of “at least nine months”, citing the 12-month ban given to Canada Women’s coach, Bev Priestman, for using drones to spy on New Zealand during the 2024 Olympics, which they reduced to a suggestion of three months allowing for mitigation.View image in fullscreenTonda Eckert can continue in his role after receiving a suspended ban.Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty ImagesThe commission accepted Eckert’s evidence regarding the three incidents in question, namely that he suggested observing Oxford’s training session before a Championship game last December, accepted video footage from an Ipswich session later in the season without commissioning the spying and requested that someone watch Middlesbrough train before the playoff semi-final to determine whether Hayden Hackney was fit to play.Eckert’s claim that he did not know such acts were a breach of EFL regulations was also accepted by the commission, which concluded that a 16-week ban from football was proportionate before mitigation.The commission noted what they described as Eckert’s “genuine contrition”, however, including consulting a psychologist to determine how his behaviour could affect other members of staff, and the fact that a lengthy ban would almost certainly cause him to lose his job, which led to their proposed ban being reduced to nine weeks.A further three-week reduction was applied in recognition of Eckert’s guilty plea before the commission opted to make the six-week ban suspended because of the wider impact such a punishment would have on Southampton as a club and their fans.In response to the verdict, the Southampton chair, Dragan Solak, gave his backing to Eckert and praised the FA’s handling of the process, but was extremely critical of the EFL. “We have already suffered enough, and we appreciate the panel’s recognition of that,” Solak said. “We are confident the manager has learned from this matter, and a suspended sentence allows him to continue in his role.“I firmly believe that Tonda is one of Europe’s most exciting young coaches, and with this distraction removed, I am confident he can lead the team to a successful season. I’d like to thank our fans for standing by us and showing the team so much support during a time when we have needed them more than ever.“The FA process has been a positive experience. Tonda has been given the opportunity to be open and honest with the panel, and the panel has been able to see that he is simply a good person who made poor decisions.“The same cannot be said for the EFL process, and the way they have subsequently treated us is not something we will forget. However, now is the time to look forward to what I believe will be a great future for our club.”Explore more on these topicsSouthamptonThe FAnewsShareReuse this content

title: England ready to level up and embrace ‘calculated risks’, claims Tuchel | England | The Guardian
description: Thomas Tuchel was pleased ‘everyone bought in’ to new ideas during the international window, and Jarell Quansah said England could ‘really dominate teams’
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Thomas Tuchel was pleased ‘everyone bought in’ to new ideas during the international window, and Jarell Quansah said England could ‘really dominate teams’
Content: Thomas Tuchel puts an encouraging arm around Anthony Gordon after England’s 3-0 win against Czechia at Wembley.Photograph: Robin Jones/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThomas Tuchel puts an encouraging arm around Anthony Gordon after England’s 3-0 win against Czechia at Wembley.Photograph: Robin Jones/Getty ImagesEnglandEngland ready to level up and embrace ‘calculated risks’, claims TuchelHead coach pleased ‘everyone bought in’ to new ideasJarell Quansah says: ‘We can really dominate teams’David HytnerWed 7 Oct 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 7 Oct 2026 15.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel believes England have unlocked a new level after moving forward with his tactical tweaks in the openingNations Leaguefixtures. The head coach wanted the players to retain their aggression, especially in the high press, to step on to the front foot and to harness the chaos often seen in the Premier League. But he has also tried to get them to play with greater freedom, to trust and follow their instincts more – while being alive to the need to cover for their teammates.The results have been positive. Afterlosing to Spain at Wembley, England recorded three wins: twoagainst Czechiaeither side ofthe 7-0 victory against Croatiain Rijeka. They have in essence guaranteed their progress into the quarter-finals of a competition regarded as a tune-up for Euro 2028, while putting a bit of distance between themselves and the heartbreakingWorld Cup semi-final defeat by Argentinain July.All aboard the Tuchel train? England camp has clear winners and losersRead more“I have never done a big tournament or a big camp after a tournament,” Tuchel said. “It was new for me and brilliant to see how everyone bought in to the idea of the next steps and the details needed to adjust to maybe unlock the next level.“It was football on a very high level, football that suits us, attacking football. It was a lot of high-ball wins and we took some calculated risks in the ‘man-man’ approach in the opponents’ half. We did it in all four games and we had four good performances if unfortunately not four wins. We didn’t beat Spain but it was always about the reaction and that was on a high level.”Tuchel’s assistant, Anthony Barry, talked on Monday about adding more flexibility and fluidity to the game model. Tuchel was asked to elaborate. “We had the feeling that it was the next step because we saw them in training and we said sometimes we were missing the transfer [from the training pitch] into the game,” he said.“So we made some slight adjustments to how we trained – not big ones because we always believed we had something to build on – but slight adjustments in the structure of how we build up and also how we defend. I am happy that what we did worked. We finally had two weeks with the team which helped a lot because we can do reviews of matches and training and we have a chance for a common language to sink in, for the patterns to sink in.”View image in fullscreenJarell Quansah has urged his England teammates to be ‘relentless and ruthless’.Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty ImagesThe defender Jarell Quansah said the style had evolved since the World Cup and felt more aggressive and front-footed. “It’s exactly that,” he said. “I think it’s going all out. We can really dominate teams with the lads playing in the Premier League at such a high level and high intensity.“It’s being relentless and ruthless. As soon as we score a goal, it’s not easing off, it’s going again, going again, trying to get the next goal, trying to put the next player under pressure. Everyone’s working for each other. If someone gets outplayed, the next person is into a tackle.“We’ve put together a few performances now where we’ve fully gone for games and not tried to sit back. That’s what we wanted to do in this camp. We’ve shown how aggressive and dominant we can be against top nations in a tough group. There’s a lot more to come.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuansah also opened up on the pain of his World Cup red card. He was sent off in the last 16 against Mexico at the Estadio Azteca for catching Jesús Gallardo with a high and late tackle. It was the 54th minute and England led 2-1. They went further in front before being pegged back to 3-2 and digging infor a famous victory. Quansah was suspended for the quarter-final and semi-final.“It was horrible,” he said. “I went into the tackle quite fast so it was a bit unlucky to end up the way it did. Being inside [the dressing room] and watching the team pull through was gut-wrenching but an unbelievable moment as well.“It was tough. And obviously the two-game ban wasn’t ideal. You’re not just going to move on and forget about stuff. Obviously, it hurts so much. It’s not easy to get over something like that and it’s not been too long after.”Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelNations LeagueFootball tacticsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Demand for Springboks and All Blacks Twickenham tickets outstrips hosts England | Nations Championship | The Guardian
description: Demand for South Africa and New Zealand tickets for the Nations Championship finals weekend has been greater than those for England
Author: Gerard Meagher
Headline: Demand for South Africa and New Zealand tickets for the Nations Championship finals weekend has been greater than those for England
Content: Rugby fans at Twickenham, where six rankings matches will all take place next month.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPAView image in fullscreenRugby fans at Twickenham, where six rankings matches will all take place next month.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPANations ChampionshipDemand for Springboks and All Blacks Twickenham tickets outstrips hosts EnglandSouth Africa and New Zealand tickets sold out for finals weekendEngland lost 42-21 to Ireland in team’s last Twickenham gameGerard MeagherWed 7 Oct 2026 08.28 EDTLast modified on Wed 7 Oct 2026 18.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDemand for South Africa and New Zealand tickets for theNations Championshipfinals weekend has been greater than those for England despite Twickenham hosting the inaugural competition’s finale.Six rankings matches will all take place at Twickenham next month – two on Friday, two on Saturday and two on Sunday – in a culmination of the competition’s first edition. The grand finale on Sunday pits the top nation in the northern hemisphere pool against their southern counterparts. Second plays second, third plays third and so on.Tickets are available for each day, as are bundles for all three days, or two of the three. To guarantee a ticket for a particular nation’s rankings match, “support your team” tickets can also be bought.The Breakdown | Nations Championship fails to solve rugby’s ability to get in the way of itselfRead moreThose for South Africa, the winners of the past two World Cups and top of the southern hemisphere table at the halfway point, as well as New Zealand have sold out. But those for England were still available on Wednesday for £164.80. Tickets were also still available at the same price for the other nine competing nations.In total, 60-65% of tickets have been sold for finals weekend following a spike in interest after the July fixtures with organisers bullish that their promise to stage a “festival of rugby” is resonating.England play three pool matches – against Australia, Japan and New Zealand – before the finals weekend, which may explain why demand has been higher to see the Springboks and the All Blacks in action. England’s last appearance at Twickenham was calamitous, however, a42-21 defeat by Irelandduring their worst Six Nations campaign.View image in fullscreenA mainly South African crowd watch the Argentina ‘home’ game during the Rugby Championship at the Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianTwickenham has come to be a home from home for South Africa, who have appeared there in fixtures against Argentina, Wales and New Zealand in recent years. There is a sizeable New Zealander expat population in London and the Springboks’ thumping 2023 World Cup warm-up win over the All Blacks was witnessed by a crowd of more than 80,000.That was the last Test held at Twickenham on a Friday night and theRugby Football Unionwill be anxious to see how November’s double header plays out. The union is awaiting Richmond council’s decision over its planning application to host more concerts at Twickenham.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAccording to submissions by residents in opposition to the RFU’s proposal, that Friday night match between South Africa and New Zealand was blighted by numerous examples of antisocial behaviour. Richmond council was initially due to return its decision this week but the worry at the RFU is that it will not do so until after this November’s Nations Championship fixtures.Meanwhile, the England assistant coach Joe El-Abd will leave his position after next year’s World Cup to take up a post with Clermont. El-Abd, a close confidant of Borthwick, joined the setup in the autumn of 2024, initially as defence coach.A year later, El-Abd was demoted to assisting with the forwards and contact skills. He has been regularly linked with a return to France – he was previously the director of rugby at Oyonnax – and is now set to do so at the culmination of England’s campaign in Australia next year.Explore more on these topicsNations ChampionshipEngland rugby union teamSouth Africa rugby teamNew Zealand rugby union teamRugby Football UnionRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content

title: Fifa reportedly allowed DR Congo into World Cup despite ineligible player in qualifying | World Cup 2026 | The Guardian
description: Fifa allowed the Democratic Republic of the Congo to compete at this summer’s World Cup despite reports suggesting an internal investigation found that the country had fielded an ineligible player in qualifying
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: Fifa allowed the Democratic Republic of the Congo to compete at this summer’s World Cup despite reports suggesting an internal investigation found that the country had fielded an ineligible player in qualifying
Content: Lionel Mpasi played a key role for the Democratic Republic of the Congo at this summer’s World Cup.Photograph: Daniel Becerril/ReutersView image in fullscreenLionel Mpasi played a key role for the Democratic Republic of the Congo at this summer’s World Cup.Photograph: Daniel Becerril/ReutersWorld Cup 2026Fifa reportedly allowed DR Congo into World Cup despite ineligible player in qualifyingNigeria filed complaint over ineligible players in playoffFifa investigators aware of situation before tournamentPaul MacInnesWed 7 Oct 2026 06.28 EDTFirst published on Tue 6 Oct 2026 14.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFifa allowed the Democratic Republic of the Congo to compete at this summer’sWorld Cupdespite reports suggesting an internal investigation found that the country had fielded an ineligible player in qualifying.The player in question, the goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi, starred for his nation at the tournament, including againstEngland in the last 32. Mpasi, who was born in France and played forLes Bleusat youth level, had never completed the process of switching nationalities, Fifa reportedly found. No punishment was levied against the Congolese federation, Fecofa.Lionel Messi has completed football and can bid Argentina farewell with prideRead moreThe news willagain raise questionsover the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, with a series of governance scandals having brought heightened scrutiny on his position. Fifa’s investigative teams are independent and the president has no input into their proceedings. Fifa is understood to have denied that Infantino played a part in the decision-making process over Mpasi, but his name is likely to remain in focus owing to a former university associate, Véron Mosengo-Omba, being elected unopposed as president of Fecofa this May.The Nigerian Football Federation submitted a complaint over the DRC apparently fielding ineligible players during a World Cup playoff tie between the nations, which the DRC won on penalties, in November.According to reporting by the New York Times and Le Monde,Fifainvestigators were aware of Mpasi’s situation before the DRC defeated Jamaica in a final intercontinental playoff round in March. Faced with a series of possible responses, including banning the DRC from the playoffs, Fifa chose to reject the Nigeria complaint on the grounds it had not been submitted within the necessary timeframe.Nigeria appealed against the decision and government representatives have suggested they could seek financial compensation for their loss, with a member of the national sports commission , which regulates Nigerian sport, telling ESPN: “Nothing has been decided yet, but we will seriously consider seeking compensation from Fifa for all of the economic losses this has cost Nigeria.”Concacaf, the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, which includes Jamaica among its members, said it “takes player eligibility matters very seriously and expects the applicable regulations and procedures to be applied consistently and fairly in all competitions”. In a statement it asked that any “concerns regarding player eligibility” be “thoroughly reviewed and addressed through Fifa’s appropriate governance and disciplinary bodies”.A Fifa spokesperson said: “Fifa can confirm that there were no eligibility issues for DR Congo’s matches against Jamaica and at the subsequent FifaWorld Cup 2026. As outlined, the Fifa disciplinary committee dealt with a protest filed by the Nigeria Football Federation, which was ruled inadmissible.”Caf, the Nigeria Football Federation and Fecofa were approached for comment.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOn Tuesday the Norwegian football federation confirmed it had submitted a three-pronged complaint to Fifa over its governance, including the decision tooverturn a red cardawarded to the USA’s Folarin Balogun after a telephone intervention by Donald Trump. The other instances cited by the NFF are the Fifa peace prize and the abandoned plan to sell a share in the World Cup to investors, known as theFifa Forward Enterprise scheme.“Each of these cases must be assessed based on the facts of each individual case,” said the president of the NFF, Lise Klaveness. “At the same time, the cases point to a more fundamental question: has Fifa’s position, authority or influence been used in a way that was not appropriate, and if so, did the mechanisms that were supposed to prevent this function work as they should?”Explore more on these topicsWorld Cup 2026FifaDemocratic Republic of the Congo football teamGianni InfantinoWorld CupFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City’s glory cannot be taken away from the players, says Kyle Walker | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Manchester City’s glory years cannot be taken away from the players insists former captain Kyle Walker.
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Manchester City’s glory years cannot be taken away from the players insists former captain Kyle Walker.
Content: Kyle Walker, right, celebrates winning the 2024 Premier League title with Manchester City, one of 12 major domestic honours he won at the now disgraced club.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenKyle Walker, right, celebrates winning the 2024 Premier League title with Manchester City, one of 12 major domestic honours he won at the now disgraced club.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianManchester CityManchester City’s glory cannot be taken away from the players, says Kyle WalkerFormer captain admits guilty verdict ‘doesn’t look great’But he insists memories of ‘many trophies’ will remainPA MediaWed 7 Oct 2026 06.01 EDTLast modified on Wed 7 Oct 2026 11.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City’s glory years cannot be taken away from the players, despite the club beingfound guilty of all charges of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, insists former captain Kyle Walker.City have appealed against last week’s seismic judgment of an independent commission that they broke rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, with the club found to have boosted their income by a staggering amount of more than £900m. Walker spent eight years at City from 2017 to 2025, winning the Champions League as well as 12 major domestic honours. “Obviously it doesn’t look great,” said the current Burnley captain on TalkSport. “It’s in an appeal stage so for me to start commenting on the legal action … it’s not going to do myself justice or anyone involved in it.Manchester City’s ‘sham’ seasons: how they fared and who was in chargeRead more“But, at a personal level, I can say the lads, we spent many a great year celebrating many trophies and everything like that and that’s something that, whatever happens, they can’t take away from us because we’ve experienced them nights. So, whatever will be, will be, and it’s just down to the appeal now and what goes from there.”Walker conceded City’s guilty verdict is not an easy subject for former players to discuss. “It’s something we don’t want to talk about because we want to be looked upon as winning them trophies, winning them the right way,” he said. “It’s very difficult because we’ve worked very hard for them.”A City statement released last Friday read: “The club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.“The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CitynewsShareReuse this content

title: USMNT closes international window with 1-0 win over Canada – as it happened  | USA | The Guardian
description: Justin Ellis scored in the first half to cap a perfect elongated international window for Mauricio Pochettino’s side.
Author: Beau Dure
Headline: Justin Ellis scored in the first half to cap a perfect elongated international window for Mauricio Pochettino’s side.
Content: 23h ago22.17 EDTSummarySo this unusually long international window concludes, with theUSAwinning four straight games by a combined score of 12-3.Competition for places over the next three years will be simply brutal.As forCanada, Jesse Marsch and a handful of strong attackers will always be a handful for any opponent.Jeff Rueter has the recap.
